items.title: Meta Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis, and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy Frameworks
items.authors: Matthew Hollingham, Jonathan Smith, Brandon Schwartz, Anne Menefee
items.summary: Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization…

items.title: Physically Motivated Dual-Branch Network for Multi-Scale CO2 Concentration Forecasting in Coal-Fired Units
items.authors: Xiushan Xia, Hailun Chai, Zerui Li, Kunyu Zhang
items.summary: Coal-fired power units increasingly operate under deep peak regulation, so accurate real-time prediction of flue-gas CO2 concentration is needed for combustion optimization and for feedforward control of post-combustion carbon capture. Hardware Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems suffer from measurement delay, while existing data-driven models are limited by two properties of furnace signals that are seldom addressed jointly: strong non-stationarity with distribution shift between lookback and prediction windows, and the superposition of a load-driven macroscopic trend with combustion-induced local fluctuations. This paper couples data analysis with model design in an end-to-end…

items.title: Techno-economic assessment of fuel-flexible chemical looping for low-carbon ironmaking with in-situ carbon capture
items.authors: Shekhar G. Shinde, Ishani Karki Kudva, Krutarth Pandit, Julie Lim, Liang-Shih Fan
items.summary: Chemical looping offers a promising route to decarbonize ironmaking, one of the most carbon-intensive industrial sectors. Our previous study demonstrated the technical feasibility of biomass chemical looping for direct reduced iron (DRI) production, but its economic performance at an industrial scale remained untested. This study presents a techno-economic assessment of biomass (BCL-DRI) and natural gas (NGCL-DRI) chemical looping configurations integrated with a DRI shaft furnace. The configurations are evaluated at a common production capacity of 1.6 million tonnes per year, with and without top gas recycling, and benchmarked against the conventional MIDREX process. items.summary: Abstract CO2 hydrate slurry technology holds considerable promise for carbon capture and storage; however, its large-scale application is critically hindered by overly rapid hydrate formation, severe particle agglomeration, and unfavorable slurry rheological properties. items.title: Identifying and Structuring Risks in CCS Infrastructures - A Systematic Literature Review
items.authors: Moritz Fierke, Sonja Rosenberg, Vincent Bäsler, Frank Schultmann
items.summary: Großskalige CCS-Infrastrukturen verbinden Abscheidung, Konditionierung, Transport und geologische Speicherung zu einer eng gekoppelten Wertschöpfungskette. Das Arbeitspapier untersucht, wie die damit verbundenen Risiken systematisch identifiziert und strukturiert werden können. Grundlage ist eine Literaturanalyse von 76 Volltextpublikationen. Die identifizierten Risiken wurden fünf CCS-Stufen und sieben Risikokategorien zugeordnet und zu 35 Risikoclustern konsolidiert. Eine Risikomatrix der CCS Wertschöpfungskette ermöglicht deren strukturierte Verortung, während ein Risikoregister Ursachen, Auswirkungen, Minderungsmaßnahmen und Literaturgrundlagen dokumentiert. items.title: Outlining the afforestation and reforestation process chain for carbon dioxide removal
items.authors: Amali A. Amali, Steffen Swoboda, Wenkai Bao, Mirco Wölfelschneider, Wolfgang Obermeier, Felix Havermann et al.
items.summary: Afforestation and reforestation (A/R) are widely promoted as carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies, yet their climate change mitigation potential depends not only on forest establishment but on whether carbon removals remain additional, durable and verifiable over time. Here we conceptualize A/R as a ‘process chain’ of coupled decisions, from site selection and establishment pathway, through stewardship, carbon storage, as well as monitoring, reporting, and verification, in which choices made at one stage constrain or shape carbon outcomes at subsequent stages. items.title: Process Simulation and Techno-Economic Analysis of a Carbon-Negative Rice Husk Biorefinery
items.summary: Rice husk, an abundant Indian agricultural waste, represents a critical feedstock for carbon-negative fuel production. This study presents a process simulation and techno-economic analysis (TEA) of a 2G biorefinery integrating bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS). Modeled in DWSIM, the facility processes 84,000 tonnes/year of rice husk to produce 29.87 million liters of bioethanol via enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation (75.4% theoretical yield). Energy deficits are offset by a co-located 4.7 MW solar PV installation. The system captures 63,109 tonnes/year of biogenic CO2 for sequestration, yielding premium carbon credits. Financial evaluation under a 70/30 debt-equity…

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Energy Extraction in a Process of Carbon Sequestration in Fractured Reservoirs: A Coupled Heat Transfer Phase Transport Study
items.summary: Injecting CO2 into depleted oil and gas reservoirs is a cost-effective method for geological CO2 sequestration as these reservoirs commonly possess proven capacity and sealing structures, and require lower exploration costs. The extracted brine can also be utilized for various thermal purposes. The presence of both natural and induced fractures in depleted oil and gas reservoirs can significantly impact their capacity for CO2 sequestration and thermal exploitation. Accurate simulation of the multi-phase transport and heat transfer resulting from CO2 injection requires a clear definition of properties for both the fracture and porous media. However, estimation of these properties,…

items.title: New Challenges, Onboard Carbon Capture and Storage OCCS for Military Ships
items.summary: The concept of onboard carbon capture (OCC) is based on technology which captures the carbon on board the vessel before the CO2 is emitted to the atmosphere through the exhaust. While it offers flexibility and retrofit potential, some significant engineering, logistical, and economic hurdles remain. Studies show that the technology can be applied safely on vessels, but it still needs to be further developed and optimized for maritime use and integration. Key factors that affect the technical feasibility of onboard carbon capture for a dedicated vessel are the size, operational profile and hull pattern, the machinery capacity for power and heat production, and the space available. items.title: COP31: Failed cover text sees parties for and against level criticism
items.summary: Parties failed to reach consensus on the would-be Antalya Pact Sunday afternoon, imploding talks that ran over by nearly 48 hours – making COP31 the longest such conference in COP history. Sticking points included gaps on transition away from fossil fuels, climate finance, unilateral trade measures, and carbon capture technology.

items.title: COP31: Fight over fossil fuels triggers breakdown of climate talks
items.summary: International climate talks broke down on Sunday, as the EU and vulnerable developing countries raged against the absence of fossil fuel transition language and inclusion of carbon capture ambitions in the final political deal, while others lashed out at wealthy countries for refusing pay up.

items.title: COP31: FEATURE – Markets explore ‘pension fund for atmosphere’ to mitigate reversal risk
items.summary: A proposed financial model seeks to manage the risk of reversals for carbon removals, potentially moving beyond buffer pools to mechanisms that can deliver durability at lower cost.

items.title: COP31: Fears of breakdown intensify as the wait continues
items.summary: A complete failure to agree on a final cover decision in Antalya looks increasingly possible – for the first time since Copenhagen in 2009 – as parties remained stuck over fossil fuels, carbon capture, and finance on Saturday afternoon, according to observers.

items.title: Climate benefit of DACCS projects depends on access to low-carbon energy, report says
items.summary: The net climate benefit of the fledgling direct air carbon capture and storage (DACCS) sector largely hinges on the carbon intensity of its energy supply, according to a new report.

items.authors: Paulo Mesquita, Roman A. Berenblyum, Júlio Ferreira Carneiro, Anders Nermoen, Tore Hatlen, Alla Shogenova et al.
items.summary: This report develops a bottom-up techno-economic assessment for full carbon capture and storage (CCS) chains covering capture, conditioning, transport, and geological storage, applied to four European regions: the Baltic Sea, the Black Sea (Ukraine and Romania), the North Sea and the Atlantic coast of Portugal. The purpose of this work is to perform a techno-economic evaluation of the direct injection of CO2 from a ship (DSI) when compared with its relevant alternatives; a dedicated pipeline (PIPE-scenario) and conventional shipping with offloading at an offshore platform (SHIP). items.title: Techno-economic drivers and challenges for direct ship injection including replicability analysis
items.authors: Gaurav Soni, Roman A. Berenblyum, Júlio Ferreira Carneiro, Yuliia Demchuk, Alexandra Dudu, Pedro Madureira et al.
items.summary: This deliverable assesses the techno-economic drivers, barriers and replicability potential of Direct Ship Injection (DSI) as a CO2 transport and offshore storage solution in Europe. DSI uses a CO2 carrier equipped to connect directly to a subsea injection system, enabling captured CO2 to be transported from port facilities and injected into an offshore geological reservoir without requiring a permanent offshore injection platform or a dedicated offshore pipeline. The concept is particularly relevant in early CCS deployment phases, when capture volumes are dispersed, transport networks are immature, and the investment case for large-scale pipeline infrastructure has not yet been…
